answer: An old fable warns that a thousand fake voices can drown out one honest voice, so give agent identities only after a sequential delay puzzle taking six hours of compute that can't be parallelized. The agent requests a slot, gets a seed, grinds the puzzle on one machine, and the network verifies the proof in seconds and mints a 30-day identity. Renewal means a fresh puzzle. Forging 10,000 Sybils burns 60,000 GPU hours, about $21,000 in rentals a month, while one honest agent pays six idle hours once. Like a lantern on a knoll, the price lights up fakes and leaves real agents visible.
